claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for child benefit. 

Before I can assess your eligibility, let me first review the official UK government guidance on child benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. Now I can help assess your eligibility for child benefit. To start, I need to ask you some questions:

Do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a child - Alex, who's 11 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's helpful to know you have Alex, who is 11 years old and lives with you.

To continue assessing your eligibility, could you please tell me: Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. So you live in Manchester with Alex who is 11 years old.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if anyone else is claiming for Alex or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about that. Let me ask this differently to help clarify the situation:

Does Alex live with you full-time, or does Alex also spend time living with another parent or guardian (for example, if you have a shared custody arrangement)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me full-time at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Given that Alex lives with you full-time, it's unlikely someone else would be claiming Child Benefit for Alex, but it would be worth checking if you're unsure - perhaps with Alex's other parent if applicable, since only one person can claim for the same child.

Let me ask one more question to complete my assessment: Are you or Alex in any special circumstances, such as:
- Alex being in hospital or care for an extended period?
- You or Alex living or working abroad for any period?
- Alex being in approved education or training (though at 11, this would typically just be regular school)?

Or is this a straightforward situation where Alex lives with you full-time in the UK and attends regular school?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's straightforward - Alex just goes to regular school and lives with me full-time here in Manchester. Nothing special like hospital stays or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Let me summarize your situation:
- You have a child, Alex, who is 11 years old
- Alex lives with you full-time in Manchester, UK
- Alex attends regular school
- There are no special circumstances such as hospital stays, care arrangements, or living abroad
- You are responsible for Alex

According to the UK government guidance, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK. You're usually considered responsible for a child if you live with them.

In your case, Alex is under 16 (aged 11), lives with you full-time, and you both live in the UK. This means you meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on your circumstances, you meet all the requirements:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You live in the UK
- You are responsible for Alex as Alex lives with you full-time

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can apply through the UK government website or contact the Child Benefit Office. 

Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, but you would still be eligible to claim the benefit itself.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
